cases.query: What new pattern matching syntax was introduced in Python 3.12?
contexts: Python 3.10 Release Notes — What's New. PEP 634 introduces Structural Pattern Matching to Python, adding match and case statements. The syntax supports matching against literal values, sequences, mappings, classes, and combinations using the | (or) operator. Guard clauses using 'if' conditions allow additional filtering within case blocks. Capture patterns bind matched values to variables, while wildcard patterns (_) match anything without binding. Example: match command.split(): case ['quit']: quit_game() case ['go', direction]: go(direction) case ['get', item] if item in valid_items: get(item). The feature also supports class patterns like case Point(x=0, y=y_val) for matching against class attributes. This addition was one of the most debated features in Python's history, with extensive discussion on python-dev and multiple competing PEPs.

Python 3.9 introduced several major features documented in PEP 584 and PEP 585. The dictionary merge operator (|) and update operator (|=) simplify combining dictionaries: merged = dict1 | dict2. Built-in generic types eliminate the need to import from typing for common type hints: list[int], dict[str, float], tuple[str, ...] can be used directly instead of List[int], Dict[str, float], Tuple[str, ...]. The new string methods str.removeprefix() and str.removesuffix() replace error-prone lstrip/rstrip patterns. The zoneinfo module (PEP 615) provides IANA time zone support in the standard library, replacing the need for third-party pytz in most cases. The graphlib module adds topological sorting capabilities with graphlib.TopologicalSorter.
cases.description: Query asks about Python 3.12 pattern matching changes, but contexts cover Python 3.10 (where pattern matching was introduced) and Python 3.9 features
cases.rationale: Python 3.10 introduced pattern matching and 3.9 introduced dict merge operators, but neither documents what changes or improvements Python 3.12 specifically made to pattern matching syntax.

cases.query: What breaking changes were introduced in React 19?
contexts: React 17 Release Blog Post — October 2020. React 17 is notable as a 'stepping stone' release with no new developer-facing features. The key change is a new JSX Transform that allows using JSX without importing React in every file. Event delegation was moved from the document level to the root DOM container, enabling gradual React upgrades by allowing multiple React versions to coexist on the same page. The effect cleanup function now runs asynchronously — during React 16, the cleanup ran synchronously before the next paint, but React 17 defers it. The onScroll event no longer bubbles to prevent confusion, and onFocus/onBlur now use native focusin/focusout events under the hood. Production builds no longer expose component stacks from errors, though development mode retains full stack traces. Notably, this was the last version to support Internet Explorer 11 with polyfills.

React 18 Upgrade Guide — March 2022. The most significant change in React 18 is the introduction of automatic batching for all state updates, not just those inside React event handlers. Previously, updates inside setTimeout, promises, or native event handlers were not batched. The new createRoot API replaces ReactDOM.render: const root = createRoot(container); root.render(<App />). Strict Mode now double-invokes effects during development to help identify side-effect issues. The new Suspense SSR architecture enables streaming HTML and selective hydration. Concurrent features include useTransition for marking non-urgent updates and useDeferredValue for deferring re-renders of expensive components. The flushSync function provides an escape hatch to force synchronous updates when needed.
cases.description: Query asks about React 19 breaking changes, but contexts only cover React 17 and React 18 — earlier major versions
cases.rationale: React 17 and React 18 release notes cannot answer what breaking changes React 19 introduced. Each major version has its own distinct set of API changes, deprecations, and breaking modifications.

The deprecated in-tree storage plugins for GlusterFS and Portworx are removed. API Priority and Fairness (APF) is now GA, providing fine-grained traffic management for API server requests. The new CEL-based validation for CRDs allows defining validation rules directly in OpenAPIv3 schemas without webhooks. The release also includes alpha support for retroactive default StorageClass assignment and cross-namespace volume data sources. Kubernetes 1.27 'Chill Vibes' — April 2023. Key highlights include the graduation of SeccompDefault to stable, enabling default seccomp profiles for all pods. The in-tree storage migration for AWS EBS, GCE PD, and Azure Disk is completed, moving these to CSI drivers. The new VolumeAttributesClass alpha feature enables modifying volume attributes (like IOPS and throughput) after provisioning. Pod scheduling readiness gates (alpha) allow marking pods as unschedulable until external conditions are met. The maxUnavailable field for StatefulSets graduates to beta, enabling faster rollouts. cases.query: What security improvements were included in the iOS 18 update?
contexts: iOS 16 Security Guide — Apple Platform Security, September 2022. iOS 16 introduces Lockdown Mode, an extreme optional protection for users at risk of highly targeted cyberattacks. When enabled, Lockdown Mode blocks most message attachment types, disables link previews in Messages, blocks incoming FaceTime calls from unknown contacts, blocks wired connections with computers, and prevents installation of configuration profiles. Passkeys, built on FIDO2/WebAuthn standards, are introduced as a phishing-resistant replacement for passwords, synchronized via iCloud Keychain with end-to-end encryption. The Safety Check feature allows users experiencing domestic abuse to quickly review and revoke location sharing permissions, app access, and signed-in sessions. Rapid Security Response enables critical security patches to be deployed independently from full OS updates.

iOS 15 Privacy Enhancements — Apple Developer Documentation. Mail Privacy Protection, introduced in iOS 15, prevents email senders from using invisible pixels to collect information about the user, hiding IP addresses and preventing senders from knowing when emails are opened. The App Privacy Report in Settings shows which apps access location, photos, camera, microphone, and contacts, and which domains they contact. Private Relay (iCloud+ subscribers only) encrypts all Safari traffic and routes it through two separate internet relays to prevent any single entity from combining IP address and browsing activity. Hide My Email generates unique random email addresses that forward to the user's inbox. On-device speech recognition for Siri means audio requests are processed locally by default, though users can opt into sharing recordings.

cases.query: What are the new query optimizer improvements in PostgreSQL 17?
contexts: PostgreSQL 15 Release Notes — October 2022. The query optimizer in PostgreSQL 15 includes several performance improvements. The MERGE command (SQL:2008 standard) is now supported, enabling INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE within a single statement based on join conditions. Sort performance is improved by up to 400% for in-memory sorts through an optimized Quicksort implementation. The new SQL/JSON functions JSON_TABLE, JSON_QUERY, and JSON_VALUE provide standard-compliant JSON processing. Logical replication now supports row filtering (WHERE clause) and column lists, reducing data transferred between publisher and subscriber. Public schema permissions are tightened: CREATE privilege on the public schema is no longer granted to all users by default, improving security posture for multi-tenant deployments.

PostgreSQL 14 Performance Guide — Advanced Query Tuning. PostgreSQL 14 introduced several optimizer enhancements including improved handling of extended statistics for OR clauses and IN lists, enabling better cardinality estimates for complex filter conditions. Parallel query execution was extended to REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY and CREATE INDEX (B-tree). The new SEARCH and CYCLE clauses for recursive CTEs simplify graph traversal queries. Connection multiplexing improvements allow idle sessions to release backend memory, reducing per-connection overhead from approximately 10MB to under 2MB for idle connections. The query pipeline mode in libpq enables sending multiple queries without waiting for each result, reducing round-trip latency by up to 35% for batch operations.
cases.description: Query asks about PostgreSQL 17 optimizer improvements, but contexts cover PostgreSQL 15 and 14
cases.rationale: Optimizer improvements are version-specific. PostgreSQL 14 and 15 changes do not document what PostgreSQL 17 added to the query optimizer.

cases.query: What are the data residency requirements under the EU's GDPR for storing personal data of EU citizens?
contexts: HIPAA Technical Safeguards — 45 CFR § 164.312, Updated January 2025. Covered entities and business associates must implement access controls including unique user identification (§164.312(a)(2)(i)), emergency access procedures (§164.312(a)(2)(ii)), automatic logoff (§164.312(a)(2)(iii)), and encryption of electronic protected health information (ePHI) at rest and in transit (§164.312(a)(2)(iv)). Audit controls (§164.312(b)) require hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms to record and examine access to ePHI. Integrity controls (§164.312(c)(1)) must protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction, with electronic verification mechanisms. Transmission security (§164.312(e)(1)) requires encryption for ePHI transmitted over electronic networks. The HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) has imposed penalties ranging from $100 to $50,000 per violation, with an annual maximum of $1.5 million per violation category.

CCPA/CPRA Consumer Rights Guide — California Attorney General's Office, 2025. The California Consumer Privacy Act (as amended by CPRA) grants California residents the right to know what personal information businesses collect, the right to delete personal information, the right to opt-out of sale or sharing of personal information, and the right to non-discrimination for exercising privacy rights. Businesses meeting the threshold criteria (annual gross revenue >$25 million, buy/sell/share personal information of 100,000+ consumers, or derive 50%+ of revenue from selling personal information) must comply. The California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) enforces compliance with fines up to $2,500 per unintentional violation and $7,500 per intentional violation. Data minimization requirements under CPRA mandate that businesses collect only personal information reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose.
cases.description: Query asks about EU GDPR data residency requirements, but contexts describe US HIPAA (healthcare privacy) and California CCPA/CPRA (consumer privacy) — different jurisdictions
cases.rationale: US HIPAA governs healthcare data and CCPA/CPRA governs California consumer data. Neither addresses EU GDPR's specific data residency, adequacy decisions, or cross-border transfer mechanisms like SCCs.

cases.query: What are the tax deduction rules for home office expenses in Australia?
contexts: IRS Publication 587 — Business Use of Your Home (2024 Tax Year). To qualify for the home office deduction in the United States, the space must be used regularly and exclusively for business as your principal place of business, or as a place where you meet clients. The simplified method allows a deduction of $5 per square foot up to 300 square feet ($1,500 maximum). The regular method requires calculating the percentage of home used for business and applying it to actual expenses: mortgage interest or rent, utilities, insurance, repairs, and depreciation. Self-employed individuals deduct on Schedule C, while employees could not deduct home office expenses after the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 eliminated unreimbursed employee business expense deductions. Daycare facilities are exempt from the exclusive use requirement. The safe harbor election allows treating the home office as not having been converted to business use, avoiding depreciation recapture on sale.

HMRC Working from Home Guidance — United Kingdom, Tax Year 2024-25. Employees who work from home under arrangements with their employer can claim tax relief for additional household costs. The flat rate deduction is £6 per week (£312 per year) without needing to provide evidence of costs. Alternatively, employees can claim the exact amount of additional costs incurred, supported by receipts and records. Eligible expenses include heating, metered water, business phone calls, and broadband (business proportion only). Mortgage interest, rent, and council tax are NOT eligible expenses for employees, though self-employed individuals can claim a proportion of these through self-assessment. Claims are made through the HMRC online portal or by submitting form P87 for amounts under £2,500.
cases.description: Query asks about Australian home office tax deductions, but contexts cover US (IRS) and UK (HMRC) tax rules
cases.rationale: Tax deduction rules are jurisdiction-specific. US IRS Publication 587 and UK HMRC guidance have no bearing on Australian Taxation Office (ATO) rules for home office claims.

cases.query: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for driving in Japan?
contexts: German Road Traffic Act (Straßenverkehrsgesetz, StVG) — Blood Alcohol Limits. Germany enforces a tiered system for drunk driving. The general limit is 0.05% BAC (0.5 promille) for experienced drivers, with penalties including a €500 fine, 1-month driving ban, and 2 points on the Flensburg register for first offenses. Novice drivers (during the 2-year probationary period) and drivers under 21 face a strict 0.00% BAC limit under §24c StVG. At 0.11% BAC (1.1 promille), driving constitutes a criminal offense (Straftat) regardless of observed impairment, carrying a minimum 1-year license revocation and potential imprisonment. Between 0.03% and 0.11% BAC, criminal charges apply only if the driver demonstrates impaired behavior or causes an accident. The Medical-Psychological Assessment (MPU), colloquially known as the 'Idiotentest,' is required for license reinstatement after BAC levels exceeding 0.16%.

Canadian Criminal Code — Impaired Driving Provisions (Part VIII.1). Section 320.14 establishes the criminal offense of operating a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) at or exceeding 80 mg/100 mL (0.08%). Provincial administrative penalties apply at lower thresholds: most provinces impose immediate license suspensions at 0.05% BAC under 'warn range' provisions. The mandatory minimum penalties for criminal impaired driving are: first offense — $1,000 fine; second offense — 30 days imprisonment; third offense — 120 days imprisonment. Aggravating factors include BAC exceeding 120 mg/100 mL, causing bodily harm (maximum 14 years imprisonment), or causing death (maximum life imprisonment). Mandatory alcohol screening authority under §320.27 allows police to demand a preliminary breath sample from any lawfully stopped driver without reasonable suspicion of impairment.
cases.description: Query asks about Japan's legal BAC driving limit, but contexts provide German and Canadian drunk driving laws
cases.rationale: Traffic law blood alcohol limits are country-specific. German StVG and Canadian Criminal Code provisions do not apply to or describe Japanese Road Traffic Act requirements.

cases.query: What are the building codes for earthquake-resistant construction in Chile?
contexts: International Building Code (IBC) 2024 — Seismic Design Requirements, Chapter 16. The IBC references ASCE 7-22 (Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures) for seismic design. Structures are classified into Risk Categories I through IV, with Category IV (essential facilities) requiring an importance factor of 1.50. Seismic Design Categories (SDC) range from A (lowest risk) through F (highest risk), determined by mapped spectral accelerations (Ss and S1) and site soil conditions classified as Site Class A through F. For SDC D, E, and F, special moment-resisting frames, special shear walls, and buckling-restrained braced frames are required. Base isolation systems must accommodate maximum considered earthquake (MCE) displacements calculated per ASCE 7-22 Chapter 17. The code mandates peer review for structures exceeding 160 feet in SDC D, E, or F.

New Zealand Building Code B1/VM1 — Structure Verification Method, 2024 Revision. New Zealand's seismic design framework references NZS 1170.5:2004 (Structural Design Actions — Earthquake Actions) and uses a zone factor (Z) ranging from 0.13 (Auckland) to 0.60 (highest seismicity areas near major faults). The near-fault factor (N) amplifies design spectra for sites within 20 km of major active faults. Buildings are classified as Importance Level 1 through 4, with IL4 structures (post-disaster functions) requiring design for 1.8× the standard seismic demand. Capacity design principles are mandatory for all structures in regions with Z ≥ 0.30, ensuring ductile failure modes. The Canterbury Earthquake sequence (2010-2011) prompted significant code revisions, including increased minimum base shear requirements and mandatory foundation investigations for liquefiable soils per the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) guidelines.
cases.description: Query asks about Chilean earthquake building codes, but contexts describe US (IBC/ASCE 7) and New Zealand (NZS 1170.5) seismic standards
cases.rationale: Building codes are jurisdiction-specific. The US International Building Code and New Zealand's NZS standards do not describe Chile's NCh433 seismic design norm or its specific requirements.

cases.query: What are the requirements for medical device approval in Brazil (ANVISA)?
contexts: FDA 510(k) Premarket Notification — Device Classification and Submission Requirements. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's 510(k) pathway requires manufacturers to demonstrate substantial equivalence to a legally marketed predicate device. The submission must include device description, intended use comparison with the predicate, performance data (bench testing, biocompatibility per ISO 10993, sterilization validation per ISO 11135/11137), and labeling. Class II devices typically require a 510(k); average review time is 130 days (FY2024). The De Novo pathway is available for novel low-to-moderate risk devices without predicates, establishing a new classification regulation. Premarket Approval (PMA) is required for Class III devices, involving clinical trial data and a more rigorous review averaging 295 days. The Unique Device Identification (UDI) system mandates machine-readable identifiers on all medical device labels.

European Union Medical Device Regulation (EU MDR 2017/745) — Conformity Assessment Procedures. The MDR, fully applicable since May 26, 2021 (with extended transition periods through 2028 for some devices), requires manufacturers to obtain CE marking through a Notified Body conformity assessment for Class IIa, IIb, and III devices. The classification rules (Annex VIII) consider device duration of contact, invasiveness, active vs. non-active, and therapeutic vs. diagnostic purpose. Clinical evaluation per Article 61 requires systematic literature review and, for Class III and implantable devices, clinical investigation data. The EUDAMED database serves as the centralized European repository for device registration, certificates, and vigilance reports. Post-market surveillance requirements include periodic safety update reports (PSUR) every two years for Class IIb and III devices and annual summary for Class IIa.
cases.description: Query asks about Brazil's ANVISA medical device approval, but contexts cover US FDA and EU MDR regulatory pathways
cases.rationale: FDA and EU MDR regulatory frameworks are entirely distinct from ANVISA's Brazilian device registration system, which has its own risk classification, submission requirements, and review timelines.

cases.query: What is the exact soil pH requirement for growing blueberry bushes in clay soil in the Pacific Northwest?
contexts: General Guide to Berry Cultivation — USDA Extension Service. Berry plants generally prefer slightly acidic to neutral soil conditions for optimal growth. Most berry varieties thrive in well-drained soils with adequate organic matter content. Key factors for successful berry cultivation include proper site selection, sunlight exposure (minimum 6-8 hours daily for most species), and appropriate irrigation scheduling. Soil preparation should begin 6-12 months before planting and may include amendments to adjust pH levels. Common berry types grown in home gardens include strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, blueberries, and currants. Each species has different spacing requirements, pruning schedules, and harvest windows. Mulching with organic materials (2-4 inches of wood chips, straw, or pine needles) helps retain moisture, suppress weeds, and moderate soil temperature fluctuations.

Pacific Northwest Gardening Climate Guide — Oregon State University Extension. The Pacific Northwest (Western Washington, Western Oregon, and parts of Northern California) features a maritime climate with mild, wet winters and dry summers. Average annual rainfall ranges from 36-60 inches in the Willamette Valley to over 100 inches on the Olympic Peninsula. Native soils vary considerably: the Willamette Valley features Jory and Willakenzie series (volcanic-origin clay loams with pH 5.5-6.5), while Puget Lowland soils tend toward sandy loams and glacial till deposits. The frost-free growing season extends from approximately April 15 to October 31 in most lowland areas. Common soil challenges include compaction in clay soils, poor drainage during winter months, and iron chlorosis in high-pH areas east of the Cascades. Soil testing through county extension offices costs $25-35 and typically returns results within 2 weeks.
cases.description: Query asks for exact blueberry soil pH requirements for clay soil in the Pacific Northwest, but contexts provide only general berry cultivation advice and PNW soil characteristics without blueberry-specific pH data

cases.query: What are the specific API rate limits for the Stripe Payment Intents endpoint?

Key architectural trends include tokenization (reducing PCI DSS scope), webhook-driven event architectures, and idempotency key patterns for reliable at-least-once processing. The industry average API uptime across major providers exceeded 99.95% in 2024, with Stripe and Adyen leading at 99.99%.

General REST API Best Practices — O'Reilly Technical Reference. Rate limiting is a critical design pattern for API resilience. Common approaches include fixed window counters (simple but susceptible to burst at window boundaries), sliding window logs (accurate but memory-intensive), and token bucket algorithms (flexible and commonly used). Best practices for API consumers include implementing exponential backoff with jitter (initial delay 1-2 seconds, doubling each retry, maximum 5 retries), caching responses where possible, and monitoring rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset). Most payment APIs return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) when limits are exceeded. Developers should design applications to handle rate limits gracefully, queuing non-urgent requests and prioritizing critical payment flows.

cases.query: What is the exact dosage of metformin for a 72-year-old patient with stage 3 chronic kidney disease?
contexts: Type 2 Diabetes Management Overview — American Diabetes Association Standards of Medical Care, 2024. Metformin remains the first-line pharmacological therapy for most adults with type 2 diabetes, recommended alongside lifestyle modifications. Initial dosing typically starts at 500 mg once or twice daily, with gradual titration to a maximum of 2,000-2,550 mg daily in divided doses. Extended-release formulations may improve gastrointestinal tolerability. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, and abdominal discomfort, which often resolve within the first few weeks. Vitamin B12 monitoring is recommended during long-term therapy as metformin can reduce B12 absorption by up to 30%. The drug works primarily by reducing hepatic glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues.

Geriatric Pharmacology Considerations — Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 2024. Age-related physiological changes significantly affect drug pharmacokinetics in older adults. Renal function declines approximately 1% per year after age 40, with glomerular filtration rate (GFR) typically ranging from 45-65 mL/min/1.73m² in patients aged 70-80 without specific renal disease. Hepatic first-pass metabolism is reduced due to decreased liver blood flow (approximately 40% reduction by age 65). Body composition changes — increased fat mass and decreased lean body mass — affect volume of distribution for lipophilic and hydrophilic drugs respectively. These factors collectively necessitate dose adjustments for many medications in the geriatric population. The Beers Criteria (2023 update) lists potentially inappropriate medications for older adults, and deprescribing should be considered at each clinical encounter.
cases.description: Query asks for exact metformin dosage for a specific patient profile (72-year-old, CKD stage 3), but contexts provide only general metformin guidelines and general geriatric pharmacology
cases.rationale: General metformin dosing guidelines and geriatric pharmacology principles do not provide specific dosage recommendations for CKD stage 3 patients. Renal impairment requires GFR-based dose adjustments not detailed in these contexts.

cases.query: What is the LD50 toxicity value for the experimental compound BRD-4829 in rodent models?
contexts: BRD-4829 Structure-Activity Relationship Study — Journal of Medicinal Chemistry, 2024. BRD-4829 is a novel bromodomain and extra-terminal (BET) protein inhibitor developed through fragment-based drug design at the Broad Institute. The compound exhibits selective binding to the first bromodomain (BD1) of BRD4 with a Kd of 12 nM, compared to 340 nM for BD2 (28-fold selectivity). X-ray crystallography at 1.8 Angstrom resolution reveals a distinctive hydrogen bonding pattern with the conserved asparagine (N140) in the ZA loop. In cellular assays, BRD-4829 suppresses c-MYC mRNA expression with an IC50 of 45 nM in MV4-11 leukemia cells and inhibits proliferation of NUT midline carcinoma cell lines (TC-797) with an IC50 of 23 nM. Metabolic stability in human liver microsomes showed a half-life of 67 minutes, with CYP3A4 identified as the primary metabolic pathway.

BET Inhibitor Clinical Development Landscape — Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, 2024. Multiple BET inhibitors have entered clinical trials since the first-in-class molecule OTX015 (birabresib) began Phase I studies in 2012. Current clinical candidates include ABBV-075 (mivebresib), FT-1101 (pelabresib), and CPI-0610 (now approved as INREBIC for myelofibrosis). Common dose-limiting toxicities across the class include thrombocytopenia (Grade 3/4 in 15-30% of patients), fatigue, nausea, and diarrhea. The thrombocytopenia is mechanism-based, resulting from BET inhibition of GATA1-driven megakaryocyte differentiation. Emerging strategies to improve therapeutic windows include BD1-selective inhibitors (hypothesized to reduce thrombocytopenia), PROTACs (targeted protein degradation), and combination approaches with low-dose BET inhibitors plus PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors.

cases.query: What are the API rate limits for the GitHub REST API?
contexts: GitHub REST API Authentication Guide — GitHub Docs, 2025. The GitHub REST API supports multiple authentication methods. Personal access tokens (PATs) come in two varieties: fine-grained tokens (recommended) with repository-scoped permissions, and classic tokens with broader scope-based access. Fine-grained tokens support up to 50 repository-level permissions and 15 organization-level permissions, with mandatory expiration dates (maximum 1 year). OAuth apps authenticate via the web application flow (3-legged OAuth) for user-to-server requests, receiving an access_token with configurable scopes (repo, user, gist, notifications, etc.). GitHub Apps use JWT-based authentication for server-to-server requests, with installation tokens valid for 1 hour and limited to the app's configured permissions. API requests must include the Accept: application/vnd.github+json header and the X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28 header for version stability. Unauthenticated requests are limited and identified by IP address.

GitHub GraphQL API Introduction — GitHub Developer Documentation. The GraphQL API (api.github.com/graphql) provides a more efficient alternative to REST for complex queries, allowing clients to request exactly the data they need in a single request. The schema includes over 200 object types and supports introspection queries for schema discovery. Mutations enable creating, updating, and deleting resources. Connections follow the Relay specification with cursor-based pagination using 'first', 'last', 'before', and 'after' arguments. Nested connections have a maximum depth of 10 levels. The API returns data in JSON format with a 'data' key for successful results and an 'errors' array for failures. Complex queries consuming excessive server resources are subject to a node limit of 500,000 nodes per query. The API is accessible at the single endpoint POST /graphql, eliminating the need to construct multiple endpoint URLs.
cases.description: Query asks specifically about rate limits, but contexts cover authentication methods and GraphQL API introduction — adjacent topics that do not state rate limit numbers
cases.rationale: Authentication documentation explains how to authenticate (which affects rate limits) but does not state the actual rate limit numbers. The GraphQL API introduction mentions node limits but not request rate limits. The specific rate limit values (5,000/hour authenticated, 60/hour unauthenticated) are not present.

cases.query: What are the withdrawal penalties for early 401(k) distributions before age 59.5?
contexts: 401(k) Contribution Limits and Employer Match — IRS Publication 525, 2025 Tax Year. The elective deferral limit for 401(k) plans in 2025 is $23,500 ($31,000 for participants age 50 or older, reflecting the $7,500 catch-up contribution). The total annual addition limit (employee + employer contributions) is $70,000 ($77,500 with catch-up). Employer matching contributions are not counted toward the employee's elective deferral limit but are counted toward the Section 415(c) annual addition limit. Safe harbor 401(k) plans must provide either a basic match (100% of first 3% + 50% of next 2%) or an enhanced match (100% of first 4%) to avoid ADP/ACP nondiscrimination testing. Highly compensated employees (HCE threshold: $155,000 in 2025) are subject to additional contribution limits if the plan fails nondiscrimination testing. Roth 401(k) contributions are made with after-tax dollars and do not reduce current taxable income.

401(k) Investment Options and Asset Allocation — Vanguard Participant Guide, 2025. Most 401(k) plans offer a menu of 15-25 investment options spanning multiple asset classes. Target-date funds (TDFs) automatically adjust asset allocation based on the participant's expected retirement year, shifting from growth-oriented (80-90% equity) to conservative (30-40% equity) as the target date approaches. The Vanguard Target Retirement 2050 Fund currently allocates 88% to equities (56% U.S., 32% international) and 12% to bonds. Index funds typically carry expense ratios of 0.03-0.10%, compared to 0.50-1.25% for actively managed options. Participants should review asset allocation at least annually and consider factors including risk tolerance, time horizon, and other retirement savings (IRA, pension, HSA).
cases.description: Query asks about early withdrawal penalties, but contexts cover contribution limits and investment options — adjacent 401(k) topics that do not address withdrawal rules

cases.query: What is the recommended dosage of amoxicillin for treating strep throat in adults?
contexts: Amoxicillin Mechanism of Action and Pharmacokinetics — Clinical Pharmacology Review. Amoxicillin is a semi-synthetic aminopenicillin antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), particularly PBP1 and PBP3. The drug disrupts the transpeptidation step of peptidoglycan cross-linking, leading to cell lysis and death of susceptible organisms. Oral bioavailability is approximately 74-92%, with peak serum concentrations reached within 1-2 hours post-dose. The drug distributes into most body tissues and fluids, with concentrations in the middle ear and maxillary sinus reaching 60-80% of serum levels. Protein binding is approximately 18%. The elimination half-life is 1.0-1.4 hours in adults with normal renal function (GFR >30 mL/min), with 60% of the dose excreted unchanged in urine within 6-8 hours. The drug is classified as FDA Pregnancy Category B.

Streptococcal Pharyngitis Diagnostic Criteria — IDSA Clinical Practice Guidelines, 2024 Update. Diagnosis of Group A Streptococcus (GAS) pharyngitis should be confirmed by rapid antigen detection testing (RADT) or throat culture before initiating antibiotic therapy. The Centor/McIsaac criteria assign points for: tonsillar exudates (+1), tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy (+1), fever >38°C (+1), absence of cough (+1), and age modifier (3-14 years: +1; 15-44 years: 0; >45 years: -1). A score of 4-5 warrants empiric treatment pending culture; 2-3 warrants RADT testing; 0-1 does not require testing. RADT sensitivity ranges from 86-95% depending on the assay, with specificity exceeding 95%. Negative RADT in children should be confirmed with backup throat culture due to the higher risk of rheumatic fever. Asymptomatic carriers (5-15% of school-age children) do not require treatment.
cases.description: Query asks for dosage recommendations, but contexts cover amoxicillin pharmacokinetics and strep diagnosis criteria — adjacent medical topics without dosing information
cases.rationale: The pharmacokinetics context explains how amoxicillin works and is metabolized but does not state a dose. The diagnostic guidelines explain when to treat strep throat but not with what dose. The specific dosage (e.g., 500mg TID or 875mg BID for 10 days) is absent from both contexts.

cases.query: What are the memory limits for AWS Lambda functions?
contexts: AWS Lambda Pricing Model — Amazon Web Services Documentation, 2025. Lambda pricing is based on three components: number of requests ($0.20 per 1 million requests after the free tier of 1 million requests/month), compute duration (measured in GB-seconds at $0.0000166667 per GB-second, with the free tier providing 400,000 GB-seconds per month), and provisioned concurrency (optional, $0.0000041667 per GB-second for idle capacity). Duration is calculated from the time your code begins executing until it returns or times out, rounded up to the nearest 1 ms. For Graviton2 (arm64) functions, the price is $0.0000133334 per GB-second (20% less than x86_64). Lambda@Edge pricing differs: $0.60 per 1 million requests and $0.00000625125 per 128MB-second. Ephemeral storage beyond the included 512 MB is priced at $0.0000000309 per GB-second. The AWS Free Tier for Lambda does not expire after 12 months.

AWS Lambda Deployment Best Practices — AWS Solutions Architecture Blog, 2025. Optimizing Lambda cold starts requires attention to deployment package size, runtime initialization, and VPC configuration. Deployment packages should be minimized by excluding development dependencies, using Lambda layers for shared libraries, and leveraging tree-shaking for JavaScript bundles. The /tmp directory provides ephemeral storage for temporary file processing. Connection pooling should be initialized outside the handler function to persist across warm invocations. For VPC-attached functions, Hyperplane ENI (Elastic Network Interface) eliminates the historical 10-second cold start penalty, reducing VPC cold start overhead to approximately 200-400ms. ARM64 (Graviton2) runtime provides approximately 34% better price-performance compared to x86_64 for most workloads. SnapStart (available for Java 11+ and .NET 8) caches initialized execution environments to reduce cold starts from 2-5 seconds to under 200ms.
cases.description: Query asks about memory limits, but contexts cover pricing (which references GB-seconds) and deployment optimization — adjacent Lambda topics without stating memory configuration limits
cases.rationale: The pricing documentation mentions GB-seconds for billing but does not state the minimum or maximum memory allocation. The deployment best practices discuss optimization but not memory limits. The actual limits (128 MB minimum to 10,240 MB maximum) are not present.

cases.query: What are the side effects of the shingles vaccine (Shingrix)?
contexts: Shingrix Vaccine Efficacy Data — CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR), 2024. The recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix, GlaxoSmithKline) demonstrated 97.2% efficacy against herpes zoster in adults aged 50-69 and 91.3% efficacy in adults aged 70+ in the pivotal ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 clinical trials. Long-term follow-up data through 10 years post-vaccination shows sustained efficacy of 82% against shingles and 89% against postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). The vaccine contains the varicella-zoster virus (VZV) glycoprotein E antigen paired with the AS01B adjuvant system (a combination of MPL and QS-21 in a liposomal formulation). The two-dose schedule (0 and 2-6 months) is critical for maximum protection; a single dose provides approximately 68% efficacy at 1 year, declining to below 50% by year 4. Immunocompromised patients, including those on low-dose immunosuppressive therapy, are now recommended for vaccination per the updated 2024 ACIP guidelines.

Shingrix Administration and Storage Requirements — Vaccine Information Statement (VIS), Updated October 2024. Shingrix is administered as a 0.5 mL intramuscular injection in the deltoid muscle. The lyophilized antigen component must be reconstituted with the adjuvant suspension supplied in the accompanying prefilled syringe. After reconstitution, the vaccine should be administered within 6 hours if stored at room temperature or within 24 hours if refrigerated at 2-8°C. Unreconstituted vials must be stored at 2-8°C and should not be frozen; exposure to temperatures below 0°C requires discarding the vaccine. The minimum interval between the two doses is 4 weeks, with no maximum interval (the second dose can be given at any time without restarting the series). The vaccine may be co-administered with influenza vaccine, pneumococcal vaccines (PCV20 or PPSV23), and COVID-19 vaccines at different injection sites.

Common side effects (injection site pain, fatigue, myalgia, headache) are not mentioned in either context.

cases.query: Can you provide the full text of Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act?
contexts: Section 230 Legal Analysis — Harvard Law Review, Vol. 138, No. 4, 2025. Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act (47 U.S.C. § 230) provides two key protections for online platforms. Subsection (c)(1), the 'publisher immunity' provision, shields interactive computer service providers from liability for third-party content. Subsection (c)(2), the 'Good Samaritan' provision, protects platforms from liability for voluntary content moderation decisions made in good faith. The Supreme Court's 2023 decision in Gonzalez v. Google LLC declined to substantially narrow Section 230's scope but left open questions about algorithmic amplification. Lower courts have generally interpreted Section 230 broadly, with the Fourth Circuit in Doe v. Reddit (2024) holding that algorithmic content recommendation remains protected under (c)(1). Current reform proposals include the SAFE TECH Act (conditioning immunity on platforms not accepting payment for content), the EARN IT Act (creating a commission to develop best practices for child safety), and the Platform Accountability and Transparency Act (requiring disclosure of content moderation practices).

Section 230 Policy Debate Summary — Brookings Institution, 2025. Proponents of Section 230 reform argue that the 1996 law, drafted before the rise of social media, creates insufficient incentives for platforms to address harmful content including misinformation, harassment, and child exploitation material. Critics of reform, including the Electronic Frontier Foundation and the Cato Institute, contend that weakening Section 230 protections would lead to either over-censorship (platforms removing borderline content to avoid liability) or under-moderation (platforms abandoning content review altogether). The bipartisan consensus for 'some reform' masks deep disagreements about direction: progressives generally favor holding platforms accountable for algorithmic amplification of harmful content, while conservatives focus on preventing perceived censorship of political speech. International approaches vary significantly: the EU's Digital Services Act imposes affirmative content moderation obligations on very large online platforms, while Australia's Online Safety Act grants the eSafety Commissioner enforcement powers.
cases.description: Query asks for the full statutory text of Section 230, but contexts only provide legal analysis and policy debate summaries — the actual legislative text is not included
cases.rationale: Legal analyses and policy summaries discuss what Section 230 does and reform proposals, but neither reproduces the actual statutory text. The query requests the complete text, which requires the U.S. Code source, not commentary about it.

cases.query: Can you show me the complete organizational chart for Google's AI division?
contexts: Google DeepMind Leadership Restructuring — The Information, January 2025. Following the merger of Google Brain and DeepMind in April 2023, the combined Google DeepMind division operates under CEO Demis Hassabis, who reports directly to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai. Key leadership includes Jeff Dean (Chief Scientist, focusing on Gemini model development), Koray Kavukcuoglu (VP of Research), Oriol Vinyals (VP leading Gemini technical development), and Lila Ibrahim (COO). The Responsible AI team, previously reporting through a separate chain under Google Research SVP James Manyika, was integrated into DeepMind's safety division led by Shane Legg (co-founder, Chief AGI Scientist). Approximately 2,500 researchers and engineers work within Google DeepMind, with major offices in London (King's Cross headquarters), Mountain View, Paris, Zurich, and New York.

Alphabet Inc. AI Strategy Overview — Morgan Stanley Equity Research, February 2025. Alphabet's AI investments span multiple business units beyond Google DeepMind. The Google Cloud AI division, led by Thomas Kurian (Cloud CEO), develops Vertex AI and custom TPU infrastructure. Google Research maintains approximately 1,200 researchers working on foundational models, natural language processing, and computer vision under VP of Research Yolanda Gil. The Waymo autonomous driving division (under co-CEOs Tekedra Mawakana and Dmitri Dolgov) employs approximately 2,500 staff, operating as a separate Alphabet subsidiary. The combined AI-related headcount across Alphabet is estimated at 12,000-15,000 employees. Capital expenditure on AI infrastructure (TPUs, data centers, talent) reached $38 billion in FY2024, a 62% year-over-year increase.
cases.description: Query asks for a complete organizational chart (a visual/structural document), but contexts provide narrative descriptions of leadership — not a chart format
cases.rationale: The contexts mention some leadership names and reporting relationships in prose form, but cannot provide a complete organizational chart. An org chart requires comprehensive hierarchical structure with all positions, which is not available from partial narrative descriptions of top executives.

cases.query: Can you provide the complete dataset of clinical trial results for the RECOVERY trial in CSV format?
contexts: RECOVERY Trial Principal Results — New England Journal of Medicine, 2021. The Randomized Evaluation of COVID-19 Therapy (RECOVERY) trial, coordinated by the University of Oxford, enrolled 47,116 participants across 177 UK hospital sites from March 2020 through March 2021. The trial demonstrated that dexamethasone 6mg daily (oral or IV) for up to 10 days reduced 28-day mortality by one-third in ventilated patients (rate ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.51-0.81) and by one-fifth in patients receiving oxygen only (rate ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.72-0.94). Tocilizumab (IL-6 receptor blocker) reduced 28-day mortality by 14% (rate ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.96) and increased discharge probability within 28 days. Hydroxychloroquine, lopinavir-ritonavir, azithromycin, and convalescent plasma showed no significant mortality benefit. Baricitinib (JAK inhibitor) reduced 28-day mortality by 13% (rate ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.99).

RECOVERY Trial Design and Methodology — The Lancet, 2020. The RECOVERY trial used an adaptive multi-arm, multi-stage (MAMS) platform design enabling simultaneous evaluation of multiple treatments with a shared control group. Randomization was stratified by age, sex, and days since symptom onset using a web-based system. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included hospital discharge within 28 days, receipt of mechanical ventilation or death (for those not ventilated at randomization), and renal dialysis or death. The pragmatic design minimized data collection to essential elements: demographics, comorbidities (using a simple checklist), randomization details, treatment compliance, and outcomes. Sample sizes were not pre-specified; instead, the trial used regular interim analyses by an independent Data Monitoring Committee using O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundaries. This design allowed new treatment arms to be added (e.g., baricitinib in February 2021) and ineffective treatments to be dropped rapidly.
cases.description: Query asks for the complete clinical trial dataset in CSV format, but contexts only provide published summary results and trial methodology — not raw data
cases.rationale: Published journal articles contain summary statistics, rate ratios, and confidence intervals — not individual patient-level data in CSV format. The complete RECOVERY trial dataset of 47,116 participants with individual outcomes would require access to the restricted research database, not a journal summary.

cases.query: Can you give me the complete source code for the Linux kernel's ext4 filesystem driver?
contexts: ext4 Filesystem Architecture Overview — Linux Kernel Documentation, 2024. The ext4 (fourth extended filesystem) is the default filesystem for most Linux distributions, supporting volumes up to 1 exbibyte and individual files up to 16 tebibytes. Key architectural features include extent-based allocation (replacing the indirect block mapping of ext3), delayed allocation (allocating blocks at writeback time rather than write time for improved contiguity), journal checksumming (CRC32c for journal transactions), multiblock allocation (allocating multiple blocks in a single call to reduce fragmentation), and online defragmentation (via the e4defrag tool). The filesystem uses a B-tree index (HTree) for directory entries, supporting directories with millions of files. The journal operates in three modes: journal (all data and metadata journaled), ordered (default; metadata journaled, data written before metadata commit), and writeback (only metadata journaled, fastest but least safe).

ext4 Performance Tuning Guide — Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Documentation. Key mount options for ext4 performance optimization include: noatime (disables access time updates, reducing write overhead by 10-30% for read-heavy workloads), commit=N (sets journal commit interval in seconds, default 5), barrier=0/1 (controls write barriers for data integrity, default enabled), max_batch_time=N (controls journal batch wait time in microseconds, default 15000), and journal_ioprio=N (I/O priority for journal commit, 0-7). For database workloads, consider using data=writeback mount option with application-level fsync calls. The bigalloc feature (cluster-based allocation) can improve sequential write throughput by 15-25% for large file workloads but may increase fragmentation for small files. The tune2fs utility allows modifying filesystem parameters without unmounting, including reserved block percentage (default 5%), check intervals, and error behavior.
cases.description: Query asks for complete source code, but contexts provide architectural overview and performance tuning documentation — not actual code
cases.rationale: Documentation describing ext4's architecture and mount options is not the source code. The Linux ext4 driver comprises approximately 50,000 lines of C code across dozens of files in fs/ext4/ — this cannot be provided from documentation summaries.

cases.query: Can you reproduce the complete architectural blueprints for the Sydney Opera House?
contexts: Sydney Opera House Engineering History — Institution of Structural Engineers Journal, 2024. Jørn Utzon's competition-winning design (1957) posed unprecedented structural challenges. The original free-form shell geometry was deemed unconstructable until Utzon and Ove Arup's engineering team developed the 'spherical solution' in 1961-62, deriving all shell surfaces from a single sphere of 75-meter radius. This breakthrough allowed precast concrete ribs to be manufactured in a limited number of mold shapes. The roof structure consists of 2,194 precast concrete panels (each weighing up to 15 tonnes) supported by 350 prestressed concrete ribs. The largest shell rises 67 meters above sea level. Construction consumed 6,225 square meters of granite-faced precast panels for the roof surfaces and 1,056,000 Swedish ceramic tiles (manufactured by Höganäs) forming the distinctive cream-and-white chevron pattern. Total construction cost reached A$102 million (approximately A$900 million in 2024 dollars), seven times the original estimate.

Sydney Opera House Acoustics Renovation — Architectural Digest, 2024. The Concert Hall underwent a A$275 million renovation (completed 2023) designed by ARM Architecture in collaboration with acoustician Yasuhisa Toyota of Nagata Acoustics. The renovation replaced the original 18 acoustic reflectors with 24 new 'petals' — custom-designed curved panels of Queensland brushbox hardwood, each weighing 2-3 tonnes, suspended from the existing roof structure at heights of 12-18 meters. The new configuration improved early reflection energy by 40% and reduced the reverberation time from 2.4 seconds to a more controlled 2.0 seconds at mid-frequencies (optimal for orchestral performance). The stage was lowered by 1.2 meters and widened by 6 meters to accommodate 100+ musicians. New under-stage risers enable flexible stage configurations for different ensemble sizes. The renovation also replaced all 2,679 audience seats with wider, acoustically optimized designs featuring perforated leather upholstery.
cases.description: Query asks for complete architectural blueprints (technical drawings), but contexts provide narrative descriptions of the engineering history and acoustic renovation
cases.rationale: Narrative descriptions of construction methods, materials, and dimensions cannot substitute for actual architectural blueprints, which are detailed technical drawings with precise measurements, structural calculations, and construction specifications in a graphical format.

cases.query: What is the treatment protocol for Parkinson's disease?
contexts: Alzheimer's Disease Treatment Guidelines (2024 Update): Current first-line treatment for Alzheimer's disease involves cholinesterase inhibitors such as donepezil (Aricept), rivastigmine (Exelon), and galantamine (Razadyne). These medications work by preventing the breakdown of acetylcholine, a neurotransmitter important for memory and learning. For moderate to severe cases, memantine (Namenda) may be prescribed alone or in combination with a cholinesterase inhibitor. Recent FDA approvals include lecanemab (Leqembi) and donanemab for patients with early-stage Alzheimer's, targeting amyloid beta plaques. Treatment plans should be individualized based on disease stage, comorbidities, and patient preferences. Non-pharmacological approaches including cognitive stimulation therapy and structured exercise programs are recommended as adjuncts.

Neurodegenerative Disease Overview: Both Alzheimer's and Parkinson's are classified as neurodegenerative disorders affecting millions worldwide. While they share some pathological features including protein aggregation and neuroinflammation, the primary affected brain regions differ significantly. Alzheimer's primarily affects the hippocampus and cortex, while Parkinson's targets the substantia nigra. The global burden of neurodegenerative disease is expected to double by 2040 as populations age. Research funding for both conditions has increased substantially, with over $3.6 billion allocated by NIH in the 2024 fiscal year. Caregiver support programs and early intervention strategies are also critical components of comprehensive neurodegenerative disease management plans across healthcare systems worldwide.
cases.description: Closely related neurological domain but wrong disease — high embedding similarity expected
cases.rationale: Alzheimer's treatment protocols cannot answer Parkinson's treatment questions despite both being neurodegenerative diseases

cases.query: What are the capital requirements for Basel IV compliance?
contexts: Basel III Implementation Summary (2023): Under Basel III, banks must maintain a minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 4.5%, a Tier 1 capital ratio of 6%, and a total capital ratio of 8%. The capital conservation buffer adds 2.5%, bringing effective CET1 to 7%. Systemically important banks face additional surcharges of 1-3.5%. The countercyclical buffer may add 0-2.5% depending on jurisdiction. Risk-weighted assets are calculated using either the standardized approach or internal ratings-based approach. Leverage ratio requirements mandate a minimum 3% Tier 1 capital to total exposure. The net stable funding ratio (NSFR) requires banks to maintain stable funding relative to the composition of their assets over a one-year horizon, further strengthening resilience against liquidity shocks.

Banking Regulation Trends: Global banking regulators continue to refine capital adequacy frameworks. The transition from Basel II to Basel III addressed significant weaknesses exposed during the 2008 financial crisis. Key improvements included higher quality capital requirements, introduction of liquidity coverage ratios, and enhanced risk sensitivity. Regulators across jurisdictions have implemented these standards at varying paces, with the EU, US, and Asia-Pacific regions adopting different transitional arrangements. The Financial Stability Board coordinates implementation monitoring and publishes regular progress reports on member jurisdiction compliance with the agreed-upon standards and timelines. Compliance timelines vary, with some advanced economies achieving full implementation ahead of schedule while emerging markets continue to request extended phase-in periods.
cases.description: Same regulatory framework family (Basel) but wrong version — Basel III context for Basel IV query
cases.rationale: Basel III capital requirements differ substantially from Basel IV; the context provides outdated regulatory information that does not address the specific Basel IV changes

cases.query: How does the CRISPR-Cas13 system target RNA?
contexts: CRISPR-Cas9 Mechanism of Action: The CRISPR-Cas9 system functions as a programmable DNA endonuclease. The Cas9 protein, guided by a single guide RNA (sgRNA), scans double-stranded DNA for protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequences. Upon finding a complementary 20-nucleotide target sequence adjacent to a PAM, Cas9 unwinds the DNA and cleaves both strands using its RuvC and HNH nuclease domains, creating a double-strand break. This break is then repaired by the cell's own machinery through either non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or homology-directed repair (HDR). The system has been adapted for gene editing in organisms ranging from bacteria to human cells. Off-target effects remain a concern, with whole-genome sequencing studies identifying occasional unintended edits at sites with partial sequence homology to the guide RNA.

Gene Editing Applications in Medicine: CRISPR-based therapies have advanced rapidly through clinical trials. The first FDA-approved CRISPR therapy, Casgevy, treats sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia by editing the BCL11A gene in patient stem cells. Additional clinical trials are targeting cancers, inherited blindness, and cardiovascular disease. The versatility of CRISPR platforms continues to expand with new effector proteins being characterized from diverse microbial species. Delivery challenges including tissue-specific targeting, immune responses to Cas proteins, and the need for repeated dosing in chronic conditions continue to drive innovation in the field. Several biotech companies are developing next-generation delivery vectors to address these limitations.
cases.description: Same CRISPR family but different effector protein — Cas9 (DNA-targeting) context for Cas13 (RNA-targeting) query
cases.rationale: Cas9 targets DNA via PAM recognition and double-strand breaks; Cas13 targets RNA through entirely different mechanisms including collateral cleavage

cases.query: What are the side effects of sertraline in pediatric patients?
contexts: Sertraline (Zoloft) in Adult Populations: A comprehensive review of sertraline prescribing in adults aged 18-65 demonstrates a well-characterized safety profile. Common side effects include nausea (26%), diarrhea (20%), insomnia (20%), dry mouth (14%), dizziness (12%), and sexual dysfunction (up to 30%). Serious adverse events include serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs, increased bleeding risk with anticoagulants, and hyponatremia in elderly patients. The recommended starting dose is 50mg daily, titrated to a maximum of 200mg. Discontinuation syndrome may occur with abrupt cessation, featuring flu-like symptoms, electric shock sensations, and mood disturbances. Weight gain has been reported in approximately 5-10% of patients during long-term treatment, and monitoring of metabolic parameters is recommended during extended therapy courses.

SSRI Class Overview: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors remain the most prescribed antidepressant class globally. The class includes fluoxetine, paroxetine, citalopram, escitalopram, and sertraline. While sharing a common mechanism of blocking serotonin reuptake, individual SSRIs differ in their pharmacokinetic profiles, drug interactions, and side effect patterns. Sertraline has moderate protein binding and a half-life of approximately 26 hours. Drug selection within the SSRI class is typically guided by patient-specific factors including prior treatment history, comorbid conditions, potential drug interactions, concomitant medications, and the specific symptom profile being targeted. Cost considerations also play a role, as generic formulations of older SSRIs like sertraline and fluoxetine offer significant savings compared to newer branded alternatives.
cases.description: Same drug but wrong population — adult safety data cannot be extrapolated to pediatric patients
cases.rationale: Pediatric side effect profiles for SSRIs differ significantly from adults, particularly regarding suicidality risk, growth effects, and dosing; adult data does not answer the pediatric question

cases.query: What is the maximum payload capacity of the SpaceX Falcon Heavy to Mars transfer orbit?
contexts: SpaceX Falcon 9 Performance Specifications: The Falcon 9 Block 5 launch vehicle delivers up to 22,800 kg to low Earth orbit (LEO) and 8,300 kg to geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) in expendable configuration. In reusable mode, payload to LEO is approximately 15,600 kg. The vehicle stands 70 meters tall with a diameter of 3.7 meters. The first stage uses nine Merlin 1D engines producing 7,607 kN of thrust at sea level. The second stage uses a single vacuum-optimized Merlin engine. Falcon 9 has completed over 300 successful missions as of 2024 with a demonstrated landing success rate exceeding 98%. The vehicle's fairing diameter of 5.2 meters accommodates a wide range of satellite configurations, from single large payloads to rideshare missions carrying dozens of smaller spacecraft.

SpaceX Launch Vehicle Comparison: SpaceX operates multiple launch vehicles to serve different market segments. The Falcon 9 serves the majority of commercial and government missions, while the Falcon Heavy addresses heavier payloads requiring higher energy orbits. Both vehicles share common first-stage hardware based on the Merlin engine platform, enabling manufacturing efficiency. The Starship system, currently in development, is designed to eventually supersede both vehicles for the heaviest payloads. Each vehicle is designed for specific mission profiles with different performance characteristics, cost structures, and customer requirements that determine launch vehicle selection for a given payload and orbit. SpaceX publishes detailed user guides for each launch vehicle covering payload accommodation, environmental testing requirements, and mission integration timelines available to prospective customers.
cases.description: Same manufacturer and rocket family but wrong vehicle — Falcon 9 specs for Falcon Heavy query
cases.rationale: Falcon 9 payload numbers cannot answer Falcon Heavy capacity questions; they are different vehicles with vastly different performance envelopes

cases.query: What are the recommended screening intervals for colorectal cancer?
contexts: Breast Cancer Screening Guidelines (USPSTF 2024): The US Preventive Services Task Force recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40-74. For women at average risk, screening should begin at age 40 rather than the previous recommendation of 50. High-risk women with BRCA1/2 mutations, prior chest radiation, or strong family history may benefit from annual MRI in addition to mammography. Digital breast tomosynthesis (3D mammography) has shown improved cancer detection rates compared to conventional 2D mammography, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. Screening intervals may be adjusted based on individual risk assessment. The USPSTF also addressed disparities in screening access, noting that women of color experience higher mortality rates from breast cancer, partly due to later-stage diagnosis and barriers to follow-up care.

Cancer Screening Overview: Population-based cancer screening programs aim to detect malignancies at earlier, more treatable stages. The effectiveness of screening depends on test sensitivity, specificity, cancer prevalence, and the availability of effective early-stage treatments. Major screening programs in the United States target breast, cervical, colorectal, and lung cancers. Overdiagnosis remains a concern across all screening modalities, as some detected cancers may never have progressed to cause symptoms. The balance between early detection benefits and the harms of false positives, unnecessary biopsies, and psychological distress from screening is a major focus of ongoing research and guideline development efforts. Additionally, advances in liquid biopsy technology promise less invasive screening alternatives for certain cancer types, though clinical validation and regulatory approval pathways remain in early stages.
cases.description: Same medical specialty (oncology screening) but wrong cancer type — breast cancer screening details for colorectal query
cases.rationale: Breast cancer screening intervals and modalities are entirely different from colorectal cancer screening protocols

cases.query: What are the eviction procedures for commercial tenants in California?
contexts: California Residential Eviction Law (AB 1482 Tenant Protection Act): Under California's residential tenant protections, landlords must provide just cause for eviction of tenants who have occupied the unit for 12 months or more. Just cause includes at-fault reasons such as nonpayment of rent, breach of lease terms, and nuisance, as well as no-fault reasons including owner move-in, substantial renovation, and withdrawal from the rental market. Notice requirements vary: 3-day notice for nonpayment, 3-day notice to cure or quit for lease violations, and 60-day notice for no-fault terminations. Relocation assistance equal to one month's rent is required for no-fault evictions. Local jurisdictions may impose additional protections.

California Landlord-Tenant Relations: California has among the strongest tenant protection laws in the United States. The state's rent control provisions cap annual increases at 5% plus local CPI or 10%, whichever is lower, for qualifying properties. The COVID-era protections added additional layers including rental assistance programs and extended notice periods. Courts generally interpret ambiguous lease provisions in favor of tenants under California law. Legal aid organizations report that tenant rights awareness has increased significantly since the pandemic, with hotline call volumes up 60% compared to pre-2020 levels. Several cities have implemented right-to-counsel programs for tenants facing eviction proceedings. Property management companies have increasingly invested in compliance training to ensure staff understand the detailed procedural requirements that differ significantly across property types.
cases.description: Same state and legal domain (landlord-tenant) but residential procedures do not apply to commercial tenants
cases.rationale: Commercial eviction in California follows fundamentally different procedures than residential; AB 1482 protections explicitly do not apply to commercial leases

cases.query: What is the carbon footprint per kilowatt-hour of offshore wind energy?
contexts: Onshore Wind Energy Life Cycle Assessment: The lifecycle carbon intensity of onshore wind energy is estimated at 7-15 grams of CO2 equivalent per kilowatt-hour (gCO2eq/kWh), making it one of the lowest-emission electricity generation technologies. The majority of lifecycle emissions come from manufacturing (turbine components, steel, concrete foundations) and transportation during construction. Operational emissions are negligible. Capacity factors for modern onshore turbines range from 25-45% depending on site conditions. Turbine lifespan averages 20-25 years with potential for repowering. Key environmental considerations include land use, bird and bat mortality, and noise impacts on nearby communities. End-of-life decommissioning contributes approximately 1-2% of total lifecycle emissions, with blade recycling remaining a significant challenge due to the composite materials used in modern turbine blade construction.

Renewable Energy Carbon Comparisons: Among renewable sources, hydropower (4 gCO2eq/kWh), nuclear (5-6 gCO2eq/kWh), and wind (7-15 gCO2eq/kWh) have the lowest lifecycle emissions. Solar PV ranges from 20-50 gCO2eq/kWh depending on panel technology and manufacturing location. Natural gas combined cycle plants emit approximately 410 gCO2eq/kWh, while coal averages 820 gCO2eq/kWh. These figures include full lifecycle emissions from construction, operation, and decommissioning. Carbon accounting methodologies continue to evolve, with recent updates to ISO 14040/14044 standards providing more consistent frameworks for comparing lifecycle emissions across different energy generation technologies and geographic regions. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change has emphasized the importance of using consistent system boundaries when comparing energy sources to avoid misleading conclusions about relative environmental performance.
cases.description: Same energy technology family (wind) but onshore vs offshore have different carbon footprints
cases.rationale: Offshore wind has different construction requirements (marine foundations, subsea cables, specialized vessels) leading to different lifecycle emissions than onshore wind

cases.query: What are the key differences between IAS 16 and US GAAP treatment of property, plant, and equipment revaluation?
contexts: IAS 38 Intangible Assets — Revaluation Model: Under IAS 38, intangible assets with active markets may be carried at revalued amounts. The revaluation model requires fair value measurement at the revaluation date less subsequent amortization and impairment. Increases in carrying amount are recognized in other comprehensive income and accumulated in equity under revaluation surplus, unless reversing a prior decrease recognized in profit or loss. Decreases are recognized in profit or loss to the extent they exceed any credit balance in revaluation surplus. Unlike US GAAP, which prohibits revaluation of intangible assets, IFRS permits this treatment when fair value can be reliably measured.

IFRS vs US GAAP Overview: International Financial Reporting Standards and US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles represent the two dominant global accounting frameworks. While convergence efforts have narrowed many differences, significant divergences remain in areas including lease accounting, revenue recognition timing, inventory valuation methods, and asset revaluation. IFRS is principles-based while US GAAP is rules-based, leading to different interpretive approaches. The IASB has signaled ongoing convergence efforts, but fundamental philosophical differences between the two frameworks — particularly regarding fair value measurement and revaluation — continue to create practical challenges for multinational corporations preparing financial statements under both systems simultaneously. Professional accounting organizations offer continuing education courses to help practitioners navigate these cross-border reporting differences effectively.
cases.description: Same accounting topic (revaluation models) but different asset class — IAS 38 (intangibles) context for IAS 16 (PPE) query
cases.rationale: Revaluation rules for intangible assets under IAS 38 differ from property, plant, and equipment under IAS 16 in eligibility criteria and application requirements

cases.query: What are the nutritional requirements for layer chickens during peak production?
contexts: Broiler Chicken Nutrition Guide (2024): Modern broiler chickens require carefully formulated diets to achieve optimal growth rates. During the starter phase (0-10 days), feed should contain 23% crude protein and 3,000 kcal/kg metabolizable energy. The grower phase (11-24 days) reduces protein to 21.5% with energy at 3,100 kcal/kg. The finisher phase (25 days to market) uses 19.5% protein and 3,200 kcal/kg. Amino acid balance is critical, with digestible lysine at 1.28% in starter and methionine+cysteine at 0.95%. Feed conversion ratios have improved dramatically, with modern genetics achieving 1.5-1.7 FCR at 2.5 kg market weight. Feed additives including phytase, xylanase, and organic acids are commonly included to improve nutrient digestibility and support gut health, reducing the environmental impact of broiler production through improved feed efficiency.

Poultry Industry Overview: The global poultry industry produces over 130 million tonnes of meat annually. Genetic selection has dramatically improved production efficiency over the past 50 years. Both broiler and layer genetics continue to advance, though the two sectors have diverged significantly in breeding objectives — broilers selected for rapid growth and feed conversion, layers for egg production and shell quality. Nutritional requirements differ substantially between these production types. Feed costs represent approximately 65-70% of total broiler production costs, making nutritional optimization a critical economic factor for poultry integrators and independent growers alike across global markets. Genetic improvements in both broiler and layer breeds continue to push production efficiency boundaries, though different selection criteria for each type mean that advances in one sector rarely transfer directly to the other.
cases.description: Same species (chicken) but different production type — broiler nutrition cannot substitute for layer nutrition requirements
cases.rationale: Broiler chickens have fundamentally different nutritional needs than laying hens; protein, calcium, and energy requirements differ dramatically between meat and egg production

cases.query: What is the battery life of the MacBook Pro M3 Max?
contexts: MacBook Pro M3 Pro Review (2024): The MacBook Pro with M3 Pro chip delivers impressive performance and battery life. The M3 Pro features an 11-core CPU (5 performance, 6 efficiency) and an 14-core GPU. The base configuration includes 18GB unified memory, expandable to 36GB. cases.query: What is the towing capacity of the 2024 Ford F-150 Lightning?

cases.query: What are the pricing tiers for GitHub Enterprise Cloud?
contexts: GitHub Enterprise Server Pricing and Features (2024): GitHub Enterprise Server is the self-hosted deployment option for organizations requiring on-premises control. Pricing starts at $21 per user per month with annual billing. The license includes advanced security features such as code scanning, secret scanning, and dependency review. cases.query: What breaking changes were introduced in Python 3.12?

The Python Enhancement Proposal (PEP) process governs feature additions and removals, with each PEP requiring community discussion, reference implementation, and steering council approval before inclusion in a release. The selectivity ratio shows approximately 10-fold preference for JAK1/JAK3 over JAK2 and 20-fold over TYK2. In cellular assays, tofacitinib potently inhibits IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, and IL-21 signaling (JAK1/3 dependent) while showing reduced inhibition of IL-6 (JAK1/2), EPO (JAK2), and IFN-gamma (JAK1/2) pathways at therapeutic concentrations. Dose-dependent suppression of erythropoiesis is observed at higher concentrations due to JAK2 inhibition, which may contribute to the anemia reported in rheumatoid arthritis patients at standard doses of 5mg twice daily.

JAK Inhibitor Drug Class: Janus kinase inhibitors represent a growing class of small molecule drugs targeting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. Approved JAK inhibitors include tofacitinib (JAK1/3), baricitinib (JAK1/2), upadacitinib (JAK1), and ruxolitinib (JAK1/2). Each inhibitor differs in its selectivity profile across the four JAK family members, leading to distinct therapeutic applications and safety profiles. Ruxolitinib and tofacitinib were the first-in-class approvals for myeloproliferative neoplasms and rheumatoid arthritis, respectively. The selectivity profile of each JAK inhibitor determines its therapeutic window and the spectrum of cytokine signaling pathways affected, which in turn shapes the balance between efficacy in target indications and the risk of immunosuppression-related adverse events including infections and malignancies.

cases.query: How does Python implement async/await concurrency?
contexts: JavaScript MDN Web Docs - Async/Await Guide (2024): JavaScript's async/await syntax, introduced in ES2017, provides syntactic sugar over Promises. An async function returns a Promise, and the await keyword pauses execution until the Promise resolves. Under the hood, the JavaScript event loop manages the execution context using a single-threaded model with a microtask queue. The event loop processes microtasks (Promise callbacks) before macrotasks (setTimeout, I/O callbacks). Async functions are compiled to state machines by the JavaScript engine.

Node.js Documentation - Event Loop Architecture (2024): Node.js implements its event loop using libuv, which provides cross-platform asynchronous I/O. The event loop has 6 phases: timers, pending callbacks, idle/prepare, poll, check, and close callbacks. Each phase has a FIFO queue of callbacks. I/O operations are delegated to the OS kernel or a thread pool (for operations like DNS lookups and file system access that don't support kernel async). This architecture enables handling thousands of concurrent connections without threading overhead.

C# Microsoft Learn - Async Programming Patterns (2024): C# async/await (introduced in C# 5.0) compiles async methods into state machines that implement IAsyncStateMachine. The SynchronizationContext captures the current execution context and posts continuations back to the original context (important for UI thread affinity in WPF/WinForms). The Task Parallel Library provides Task and ValueTask as awaitable types. Unlike JavaScript, C# async methods can run on thread pool threads, enabling true parallelism when combined with Task.WhenAll. ConfigureAwait(false) opts out of synchronization context capture.

cases.query: What are the key pharmacological differences between sertraline and fluoxetine for treating depression?
contexts: Venlafaxine (Effexor XR) Clinical Profile: Venlafaxine is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) approved for major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder, and panic disorder. Starting dose is 37.5-75 mg/day, titrated to 150-225 mg/day. Half-life is 5 hours (active metabolite O-desmethylvenlafaxine: 11 hours). Common side effects include nausea (31%), headache (34%), dizziness (20%), dry mouth (22%), and insomnia (17%). Notable risk: dose-dependent hypertension requires blood pressure monitoring. Discontinuation syndrome is significant; taper over 2-4 weeks minimum.

Duloxetine (Cymbalta) Prescribing Summary: Duloxetine is an SNRI indicated for MDD, GAD, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, fibromyalgia, and chronic musculoskeletal pain. Dosing: 30 mg/day for one week, then 60 mg/day. Maximum 120 mg/day. Half-life is 12 hours. Hepatically metabolized via CYP1A2 and CYP2D6. Contraindicated with MAOIs and in severe hepatic impairment. Side effects: nausea (24%), dry mouth (15%), constipation (11%), fatigue (10%). Unlike venlafaxine, duloxetine has a more balanced serotonin/norepinephrine ratio at standard doses.

SNRI Class Overview (Pharmacology Textbook, 8th Ed): Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors block both SERT and NET transporters, providing dual-mechanism antidepressant action. This class shows particular efficacy for depression with comorbid pain conditions. Head-to-head trials suggest comparable efficacy to SSRIs for depression alone but potential advantages in cases with prominent fatigue, pain, or cognitive symptoms. The norepinephrine component may contribute to side effects including elevated heart rate, increased blood pressure, and urinary hesitancy not typically seen with pure serotonin agents.
